subject.title: Bug: sandbox.mode: "non-main" silently breaks sessions_spawn subagent initialization

question: Should sandboxed subagent startup failures stay in the accepted-then-async run path with a visible terminal startup-failure state, or should `sessions_spawn` validate/start the sandbox before returning `accepted`?
rationale: Both approaches can fix the silent stall, but they have different compatibility, latency, lifecycle-event, and gateway-wait semantics that automation should not choose alone.

options.title: Terminalize async startup failure
options.body: Keep the current accepted-run model, but emit/log a typed startup failure that updates session, subagent, and gateway wait state when sandbox startup fails.

options.title: Preflight before accepted
options.body: Start or validate the sandbox before returning `accepted`, trading clearer immediate failure for extra latency and a stricter spawn contract.

options.title: Route through lifecycle tracker
options.body: Keep this issue as the sandbox proof case while https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/58776 owns the broader `first-progress`/`startup-failed` lifecycle design.

recommendation.title: Terminalize async startup failure
recommendation.body: Keep the current accepted-run model, but emit/log a typed startup failure that updates session, subagent, and gateway wait state when sandbox startup fails.

likelyOwner.reason: This is a cross-runtime lifecycle and subagent contract decision, and steipete has the strongest current routing signal among the likely owners.
